scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The imported polygon is in present Oklahoma, but its 1492 to 1500 interval predates Seminole removal and settlement there by centuries. No imported founding date or precise territorial boundary is certified.
The account is distinct from the Florida Seminole and Miccosukee governments. Band names and the spelling variants Mekasukey and Mekusukey are preserved in the sources.
The 1969 constitutional ratification is not confused with the 1970 council reorganization in the OHS account. The narrative avoids claiming that the Nation legally ceased to exist in 1898 or 1907.
School catalogue descriptions were read; the underlying microfilm was not. No individual pupil’s confidential history, abuse experience or unexamined record content is asserted.
OHS sources differ on the exact date when girls joined Mekasukey. The card does not repeat a disputed consolidation year. Emahaka’s 1894 opening and Mekasukey’s 1891 opening are treated separately.

The historical Arts Council teaching text and memorial notice were read in indexed form; older URLs may redirect after the agency migration. The current self-guided tour provides an accessible identification of The Guardian and its interior replica. Conflicting published weights are omitted.
The Capitol location is outside the imported Seminole polygon and is identified as the display location of a named artist’s work, not Seminole territorial control.
Historical treaty provisions are summarized as past events, without claims about current citizenship eligibility or jurisdiction. Independent review and depth certification remain pending.
